s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of shortness of breath and systemic symptoms following chemotherapy and immunotherapy
salient_findings: Shortness of breath
Loss of appetite and weight loss
Elevated cardiac biomarkers (CK, CK-MB, cTnT, NT-ProBNP)
Pericardial effusion and poor diastolic function on cardiac ultrasound
Myocardial edema on cardiac MR
key_facts: Hospitalized due to repeated cough for 2 months
No history of autoimmune diseases, diabetes, hypertension, coronary disease, arrhythmia, chronic heart failure or smoking
Experienced shortness of breath, loss of appetite and weight loss one week after 5th cycle of chemotherapy and immunotherapy
Breathing sounded normal in both lungs, without moist or dry rales
Heart rate was 115 bpm with normal rhythm
Cardiac troponin T (cTnT): 2230 ng/L (Reference range 0-14 ng/L)
Cardiac Color Ultrasound: Enlarged aorta, normal left ventricular systolic function, poor diastolic function, small amount of pericardial effusion

shortlist.label: Immune-related myocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Recent chemotherapy and immunotherapy, elevated cardiac biomarkers (CK, CK-MB, cTnT), and myocardial edema on cardiac MR

shortlist.label: Cardiotoxicity from chemotherapy
shortlist.why_kept: Recent chemotherapy, elevated cardiac biomarkers (CK, CK-MB, cTnT), and poor diastolic function on cardiac ultrasound

shortlist.label: Myopericarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Pericardial effusion on cardiac ultrasound, elevated cardiac biomarkers (CK, CK-MB, cTnT), and recent chemotherapy and immunotherapy

shortlist.label: Stress cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of shortness of breath and systemic symptoms, elevated cardiac biomarkers (CK, CK-MB, cTnT), and normal coronary artery CTA

shortlist.label: Pericarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Pericardial effusion on cardiac ultrasound, elevated cardiac biomarkers (CK, CK-MB, cTnT), and recent chemotherapy and immunotherapy

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of shortness of breath, loss of appetite, and weight loss occurred one week after the 5th cycle of chemotherapy and immunotherapy, and laboratory tests showed significantly elevated CK, CK-MB, and cardiac troponin T, indicating myocardial damage. The cardiac MR also showed myocardial edema, which is consistent with immune-related myocarditis.

rejected.label: Cardiotoxicity from chemotherapy
rejected.why: While chemotherapy can cause cardiotoxicity, the timing and laboratory findings are more suggestive of an immune-related reaction.

rejected.label: Myopericarditis
rejected.why: The presence of pericardial effusion and myocardial edema suggests involvement of both the pericardium and myocardium, but the primary issue appears to be myocardial.

rejected.label: Stress cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: There is no clear stressor identified, and the laboratory findings are more indicative of an inflammatory process.

rejected.label: Pericarditis
rejected.why: While there is a small amount of pericardial effusion, the primary findings suggest myocardial involvement rather than isolated pericarditis.
